reference_use.conclusion: The split is appropriate for the selected truncated-compactness theorem. All ten child types and the parent type elaborate independently of child implementations. The conditional parent and truncation assemblies compile using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. All six reused declarations have identical accepted frozen types, preserve the frozen definitions, and independently pass the same axiom check. The four new names are unreserved; all names are bare identifiers. Dependencies are correctly directed and acyclic, including the reused declarations' dependency closures. The snapshot contains no proved Federer–Fleming or deformation theorem available for reuse: the Ch06 contract only packages these as propositions under its unfinished main theorem. The supplied closure proof explicitly states its source results and supplies the intervening argument. Supplementary bibliographic confirmation: [White (1989), pp. 207–220](https://eudml.org/doc/140150).

nodes.reason: The one-line type matches all hypotheses and the uniform conclusion. The cutoff derivative estimate, orthonormal-frame bound, boundary cancellation, explicit integrable majorant, and Tonelli–Fatou argument produce one radius valid for every test form and bound s. Only the declared Gram-bound dependency is used.

The representation restriction supplies the required current on univ. Support agreement proves interior boundary vanishing; the mass identity proves domination and finite total mass; radial_slice proves finite boundary mass. Every conclusion follows from the listed dependencies, as independently confirmed by the compiled conditional assembly.

The statement and type agree for arbitrary P and n. Countable approximation on compact balls, diagonal extraction, and uniform mass estimates establish convergence on every test form. The final estimate proves the exact sequential-continuity field required of GeometricCurrentOn, without assuming compactness of integer multiplicity currents.

The type includes the required positive-codimension hypothesis. The induction is non-circular: CL(0), then CL(d) implies BR(d), and CL(d) together with BR(d) implies CL(d+1). Localization, slice convergence, lower density, tangent-plane construction, rectifiability, and integrality are supplied with their needed hypotheses. Deformation is used within its stated range. The unaccepted declaration from another branch appears only in a conditional reuse remark.

The remaining representation fields follow directly from the stated measurability, positivity, integrability, and containment assumptions; openness is unnecessary.
